units.text: Synaptic plasticity is the capacity of a synapse to change its effectiveness as a result of activity and other influences. Long-term potentiation, often abbreviated as LTP, refers to a lasting increase in synaptic strength, while long-term depression, or LTD, refers to a lasting decrease. At some excitatory synapses in the hippocampus, NMDA receptors help link coincident activity to calcium entry into the postsynaptic neuron. The size and timing of this calcium signal can engage different signaling pathways that influence receptor trafficking and synaptic strength.
